title: Lazy Structs (Structural Ghosts)
pattern: A struct with no fields (or only static, unused dependencies) containing only a single simple method that could easily be implemented as a pure function.
why_bad: Forces unnecessary instance creation, allocation, or dependency management merely to invoke a simple check. It clutters the workspace with structural boilerplate that does not pay for its maintenance costs.
detection: Identify stateless structs containing no member fields that are instantiated at the call site solely to invoke a single non-generic method.
counterexample: Helper structs implementing marker traits or serving as dispatch targets for generic trait boundaries (e.g., zero-sized types used in type-state pattern).
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Lazy Class" (p. 68); *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 6, "Working Classes".
